persona.who: 63, retired school principal in Chennai, husband alive, only son in Germany for 9 years with a German wife, visits every 2 years. Hindi is weak; English and Tamil.
persona.note: my son has been in germany nine years. his wife is german, lovely girl. they will not come back I know this. I taught 2000 children and I cannot teach my own heart to stop waiting for him

understanding.core_struggle: A retired teacher whose son is abroad and whose heart will not stop waiting for him, even though they will not return.
understanding.mirror: You taught thousands, but your own heart will not learn to stop waiting.
understanding.insight: It isn't the distance that keeps you up. It's the bond that was real, and the grief that has nowhere to go because you are still waiting for a door that will not open.

queries.hook: The weight of a bond that is real, and a heart that will not stop waiting for a return it already knows will not come.
queries.diagnose: Grief is love with nowhere to go; everything that comes together must part, and the mind is never still when it keeps waiting for what is gone.
queries.steady: What is real in us cannot be taken away; the love you gave and received is yours forever, and it is not diminished by distance.
queries.act: Let the love go where it can go; sit with what is real, and give your heart a place to rest that is not a waiting room.
queries.story: A parent who loved a child far away, who waited through seasons, and who one day found a way to hold the love without the waiting.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that his mind is as hard to hold as the wind, turbulent and stubborn. Krishna agrees. He says the mind is difficult to master, but through practice and letting go, it can be trained. You know this restlessness well. It moves through your nights and days with a force that feels beyond your reach.
verse.for_you: When you lie awake waiting, you are trying to hold a mind that will not be held. Today, let the waiting be there without trying to stop it. Let the mind move like the wind, and rest your attention on the one steady thing in front of you. Let that be enough for now.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth.
verse.sanskrit: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि कोऽन्वहं किमिहास्थितः / कस्मात्किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः
verse.line: In grief, ask: where did I come from, where am I going, who am I? Let that steady you.
verse.translation: 'Where was I before? Where will I go? Who am I, really, and why am I here? Why should I grieve, and for what?' Ask these, and steady the mind.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.
verse.misuse: These questions are for steadying grief, not for dismissing it; mourning is natural.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.meaning: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth. Ashma says to ask where you came from, where you are going, and who you are. These questions steady the mind. Days do not return. Grieve what is lost, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.
verse.for_you: You are asking the same question as someone who has lost everything. Today, ask yourself where you came from before this waiting began. Then ask who is still here with you, in this room, in this life. Let those answers steady you for a moment.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verse.line: Even if you believe life simply begins and ends, there's still no need to be crushed by grief.
verse.translation: And even if you think of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, still, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve like this.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Grief is human; this asks you not to be destroyed by it, not to stop feeling it.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in the middle of a battlefield, refusing to lift his bow. Krishna speaks to him of the part of a person that never comes into being and never passes away. He tells Arjuna that even if he sees the world as a place of endless birth and death, he should not be crushed by grief. The truth is, what you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain. The grief is real, but it need not destroy you.
verse.for_you: The waiting wakes you in the night, yet the love itself is not the wound. The part of you that loved your son is still whole, outlasting this long separation. Let the waiting be what it is, but do not let it become the only thing that teaches you how to live.

verse.speaker: Rahim
verse.sanskrit: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥
verse.line: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
verse.translation: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.

matched.label: My parents are getting older far away

verse.meaning: Rahim is sitting with you, looking back at the ones who have gone. He says that remembering is a kind of nearness. The people who were separated meet again, and he tells you that this is why God takes birth. When you call your son to mind, you are not just holding a memory. You are meeting him in the only way left, in the quiet of your heart.
verse.for_you: When you lie awake tonight, let the memory come. Do not try to change it or push it away. Let it sit with you like an old friend who has not left the room. That is your nearness now.

verse.speaker: Kausalya
verse.setting: Kausalya, choosing not to hold her son back, sends him into exile with her blessing.
verse.sanskrit: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
verse.line: I won't hold you back with false affection. Go, son. Just don't forget your mother.
verse.translation: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
verse.why: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

prasang.title: Kausalya lets her son go
prasang.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.
prasang.story_hook: She had the sweets ready for his coronation when he came to say goodbye.
prasang.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

verse.meaning: Kausalya is preparing to bless her son Ram as he leaves for exile. She tells him she will not hold him back with false affection. She blesses his path, asking only that he keep the bond of a mother and not forget her. She speaks these words knowing she may never see his face again.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for a return that will not come. Today, sit with Kausalya and bless your son's life from afar. Let your love be a quiet light, not a chain. Let the waiting go, and let your heart rest in the truth of what was.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: Rama is sitting alone, and Lakshmana has come to him. Rama tells him to sit in a quiet place, let the senses rest, and give his full attention to one thing. He says to keep faith until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and until he sees the divine everywhere.
verse.for_you: Find a quiet corner, let your mind rest, and give your full attention to one thing. Let your faith carry you until your mind becomes still, and see the divine in the quiet of your own heart.

story.story_hook: Two mothers, two sons gone to the same forest, and one of them found the strength to comfort the other.
story.summary: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.
story.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.

anchor.setting: Ram has left for fourteen years; his mother cannot stop weeping, and her co-queen sits with her.
anchor.sanskrit: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
anchor.line: You will see him again. Let go of this grief.
anchor.translation: You will see him again, back from the forest. Let go of grief and confusion, my queen. I tell you the truth.

story.teaser: Both their sons were gone, and Sumitra found the strength to comfort Kausalya
story.for_you: You are waiting alone in a room that holds no one. Let someone who knows the shape of your loss sit with you. Share your waiting without fixing it.

script: You have spent your life teaching children how to focus. Now the one mind you cannot teach is your own. It keeps returning to your son, to the life you imagined for him, and it will not settle. You are tired of this waiting.
Arjuna stands on a battlefield, his body trembling, his mind scattered by grief. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna does not promise the mind will stop moving. He says it is restless, stubborn and strong. The work is not to force it into stillness, but to train it through letting go. You cannot hold the wind in your hand, but you can learn to rest in the open air. This is easier said than done, because waiting feels like the only way to keep him close.

When you lie awake tonight, do not fight the waiting. Let the mind move like the wind. Rest your attention on one steady thing, the sound of your own breath, or the weight of the blanket on your chest. Let that be enough.
Can you let the wind blow, and still stand in it?

depth.life: You lie in the dark, your body still from teaching for so long, and your mind is a student that will not be quiet. It runs through every memory of your son, every message, every goodbye, and you watch it, trying to catch it, but it slips away again.
depth.points: The mind is not your enemy. It is a force, like the wind, and you cannot command it to stop. The struggle is not in the thoughts themselves, but in the effort to hold them still. The wind does not need to be held to exist.
depth.practice: Sit with your tea in the morning. Watch your thoughts move across the room like clouds. Do not name them or stop them. Just let them pass, and return your gaze to the warmth of the cup.
depth.question: What would change if you let the wind blow through your mind without trying to hold it?
